body:
**Do not merge: awaiting approval of https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/commit/f11bef695, which edits three existing tests.**

## Why

Every repository in the organisation resolves Maven dependencies through [build-kotlin-jvm](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/build-kotlin-jvm), which uses this fork's coursier-cache with one shared download directory per machine for all builds running at once. The owner asked for kompile's shared build caches to be made safe for concurrent runs and the defects fixed upstream, so that no campaign needs an external build lock. This pull request fixes one of those defects at its source.

A reproduction in build-kotlin-jvm (test on branch `repro/shared-download-after-failed-first-fetch`, commit https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/build-kotlin-jvm/commit/6c0079d6b2670e1252a9b01e0c2dab6eb970f11c, consumer draft pull request: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/build-kotlin-jvm/pull/98) starts three real resolver processes against one shared cache. After the first build's download of a JAR fails, in 40 of 40 scenarios two other builds downloaded the same file at the same time. What a build sees: one of them fails with `NoSuchFileException` on the shared `.part` file, and in 2 of 20 runs another was handed a JAR with extra bytes appended (918132 bytes instead of 524602) and no error. Upstream issue with the same symptom, open since 2020: https://github.com/coursier/coursier/issues/1818.

## Mechanism

The mechanism is that `CacheLocks.withLockOr` deletes a download's lock file by name after releasing its lock, while another process already waiting on that lock still holds a channel on the file and keeps calling `tryLock` on it. The waiter then locks the now unnamed file and proceeds as owner, while a newly arriving process creates a new file of the same name, locks it and proceeds as owner too. Both write the same `.part` file. The evidence: in the reproduction the lock file is absent from the download directory while the second process owns the download and present again (a new file) once the third starts; the test HTTP server sees both processes' overlapping requests for the same file; and the new test below fails on `main` with the third process starting its own download while the second is still downloading.

## Fix

The lock file is no longer deleted after release, so every process contending for a download always locks the one file the path names, and at most one owns the download at a time, across every ordering of acquire, release, failure and newly arriving process.

Why this and not "verify after acquiring that the locked channel is still the file at the path, and retry if not": Java offers no API to read the identity of an open `FileChannel`, and checking the path by opening it again creates a second descriptor to the same file, whose close drops the process's POSIX record locks on Linux and macOS (the `FileLock` documentation warns about this). Keeping the file is correct on both without new timeouts, sleeps, retry limits or polling changes.

Cost: an empty `<name>.lock` file stays beside each downloaded file (and archive directory). Not covered here: a process running an older coursier that still deletes after release can still break ownership for others sharing the same cache; `CachePath.withStructureLockOnce` deletes `.structure.lock` after release in the same way (not exercised by this test, not changed).

## Existing tests edited (needs approval)

https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/commit/f11bef695 edits three `FileCacheTests` "check extra artifact" cases that assert the exact list of files in the cache directory. Their expectations encoded that a download's lock file is deleted after use, the behaviour this pull request removes.
- Before: `.foo.pom.checked`, `foo.pom` (and `.foo.module.error` in one case).
- After: the same entries plus `foo.pom.lock` and, where the module download was attempted, `foo.module.lock`. The comparison stays exact.
- With the fix commit reverted, these three cases fail again (lock files missing), together with the new test: run log `reverted.log` in the evidence branch shows 4 failures out of 7 for `FileCacheTests` plus `SharedDownloadOwnershipTests`.

## Test

`SharedDownloadOwnershipTests` runs each caller in its own JVM (`SharedDownloadOwnershipProcess`, a test-source main), because file locks do not contend within one JVM. A test HTTP server holds and releases responses to force the ordering deterministically, with no sleeps as synchronisation: A's download request is held; B starts, and its HEAD length probe proves it is waiting on A's lock file; A gets a 500; B's download request is held; C starts. C's first request must be a HEAD probe (waiting); a download request is the defect. The test then asserts A's full error text, that B and C both return the published bytes, that the server served exactly two download requests, and that no two were in progress at once.

Results, all first attempts (utest does not retry), `./mill --no-server -j1 'cache.jvm[2.13.16].test.testOnly' coursier.cache.SharedDownloadOwnershipTests`:
- Without the fix (fork `main` plus the test): 4 of 4 runs fail with `A process that arrived while another process owned the download started its own download of the same cache file (server request: GET 3, downloads in progress at once: 2); at most one process may download a given file at a time`.
- With the fix: 3 of 3 runs pass.
- Cache module suite `cache.jvm[2.13.16].test` with the fix: 215 of 215 tests pass on the first attempt (before the `FileCacheTests` edit below, the same run had 212 of 215: exactly the three listing cases described below failed).

The separate defect seen in the same reproduction, a plain 200 reply to a resume (Range) request being appended to the partial file, is already fixed on this fork's `main` by https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/commit/3788263afb4b8977cfd5ebc2a557de566e0c801c (test `server ignoring range with a full response replaces the prefix`); it only needs a publish, so it is not part of this pull request.

Evidence (logs and notes): branch `wip/CLFIX-evidence-20261127`, https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/tree/wip/CLFIX-evidence-20261127/evidence/CLFIX
